chapters.headline: POETICAL
chapters.text:
First up — Page 1, Column 1. POETICAL. From the Ohio Statesman.
An untitled piece on Erin (the "bright little island," Emmet's last prayer, "Erin yet will be free! on her soil not a slave"). Signed KAY-diz, O. L. Harper. (ALTO of the signature is "KAY-diz, OA L. Haiipf.u.") Motto line under the signature: "When my country shall have taken her station among the nations of the earth, then, and not until then, let my epitaph be written."

chapters.headline: RELIGION
chapters.text:
Next up — Page 1, Column 2. RELIGION. Religion never shines with so bright and benign a lustre as upon those who embrace it in early youth. Counsellor; sun of righteousness; never be ashamed of your religion. Signed Olin.
Fillers: first interview of Baily the astronomer and Franklin in France (half an hour of silence; a pinch of snuff refused; "very well, Mr. Baily very well indeed"); Pulsations of the Heart (Herschel's Natural Philosophy / Deluc dry pile); A gentleman's pleasure (London Quarterly Review); a man three years old at Palermo (Guiseppe Gonzaga); When is a Man drunk (New York Court of Errors: as long as he can stand on his two legs without support); a clean skin (Dr. Kitchener).

chapters.headline: A POLITICAL GEM!
chapters.text: A POLITICAL GEM!. The office has never read anything that pleased it more than the following address, delivered by Gansevoort Melville, Esq., in New York, at the great Democratic festival, on the 5th ultimo. Published in full. "Read it -- Read it!"
chapters.read: A POLITICAL GEM!. The office has never read anything that pleased it more than the following address, delivered by Gansevoort Melville, Esq., in New York, at the great Democratic festival, on the 5th ultimo. Published in full. "Read it -- Read it!"

chapters.headline: FELLOW-DEMOCRATS:
chapters.text:
FELLOW-DEMOCRATS:. Not here to mouth high-sounding phrases or deify "the mill boy of the slashes." A jubilee for the anniversary of the birth-day of Andrew Jackson. Everything for the cause, nothing for men. The Whigs' 4 March pow-wow as a celebration in anticipation of the inauguration of Henry Clay -- counting chickens before they are hatched; a dinner eaten in imagination. The orator of that evening declared that the women were with them.
The address then runs through Whig aliases (a police-court prisoner always provided with half a dozen appellations -- Jack Smith alias Tom Brown, alias Jim Jenkins -- not a local surname notice); the hybrid coon party; the Bank veto of Tyler; 1840 Harrisburg / Harrison; Andrew Jackson as the son of poor Irish parents (the father died about two years after emigration; three sons, Andrew the youngest; the Revolution; Stono; the mother's grave; New Orleans). The speech occupies the rest of page 1 and most of the first three columns of page 2.

chapters.headline: Page 2, Columns 1-3
chapters.text: Next up — Page 2, Columns 1-3. Page 2, Columns 1-3. The Melville address continues and closes. Jackson as cloud by day and pillar of fire by night; the United States Bank left to rot; "adhere to our principles and we will adhere to you." Whoever the Baltimore nominee may be -- Lewis Cass of Michigan, James Buchanan of Pennsylvania, John C. Calhoun of South Carolina, or New York's favorite son Martin Van Buren -- united support. "The sun of Truth can never set." Closing: Mr. Melville's address was heard with the greatest attention.

chapters.headline: The Bargain and Sale of 1825
chapters.text: The Bargain and Sale of 1825. The New York Tribune tries to do away with the charge of bargain and intrigue against Clay and Adams. Need of a bargain: if Clay had not transferred his friends, he could not have been Secretary of State. "A bird in the hand was worth two in the bush." Signed Statesman.

South Carolina Democracy address: send no delegates to the National Convention; remain uncommitted. Cost of two English Kings, George 3d to George 4th, four hundred millions of dollars. King of Sweden still alive, no hope, apoplexy. Planet Venus throwing a shadow. Six thousand loaves of passover bread in Philadelphia and New York. Mammoth iron steamer Great Britain built too large to pass the Bristol docks. Scotch snuff for vermin on cows. Boston shop tubes from upper stories to the cash clerk. A Defaulter: Wm. J. B. Andrews, late clerk of the House at Harrisburg, alleged $22,000. Mr. Papineau at Paris collecting materials for a history of Canada. Central railroad to Kalamazoo to be completed. Frederick Martin, President of the Phoenix Bank of Columbus, Ga., arrested in Charleston. Snow at St. Catharines, Canada, 21st ult. Statuary for the Capitol arrived at Washington.

chapters.headline: Singular Marriage
chapters.text:
Singular Marriage. The Pennsylvania Legislature have passed a special act to legalize a marriage between R. Branson and wife (ALTO "i. urunson ana wne"). He had, it appears without a knowledge of the fact, married his niece.
Why is the home of Henry Clay appropriately called Ashland? Because his hopes have ever turned to ashes. The Whig Banner at Baltimore. Three steamboats with the Ericsson Propeller (Richmond, Texas, Fall River). Death of Mrs. Anne Cole, wife of Mr. George W. Cole, Newport, R. I., frightened by a flash of lightning. James Wilson, 35, killed on the Columbiana Railroad Line near Parkersburgh, Pa., knocked off a car under a bridge. Fatal accident in a South Wales colliery: of fifty-eight persons, forty-eight drowned. Mr. Pearson shot at Baton Rouge, La. Letters from Posen, 4th inst., Polish emigrants ordered to quit Prussia. A $50 rifle made to order. Nathaniel Hart, the father of Mrs. Clay, died recently at his residence in Kentucky.

chapters.headline: DEMOCRATIC TICKET
chapters.text:
DEMOCRATIC TICKET. REPRESENTATIVE,
CHARLES WARFEL.
AUDITOR,
JOHN SHARP.
RECORDER,
MATTHEW M. SLOAN.
COMMISSIONER,
Col. DAVID FINNICUM.
DIRECTOR OF THE POOR,
JACOB HINES.
(ALTO of the county heading is "MUST Bit MtEOBiEJflEu" / "DFiNOCKATIC TICKET." Page-image crop was read as MUST BE REDEEMED / DEMOCRATIC TICKET. Last week's popular-vote notice spelled the commissioner Finicum.)
We nail at our mast head the ticket put in nomination by the democracy of Harrison county, and there it shall remain until the 2d Tuesday of October.
Cheer up, boys! "all is well!" Spring elections; in the cities the friends of Clay make a little noise, but among the hard-fisted yeomanry his name excites no more enthusiasm. Farmers finding out that a tariff which filches their hard earnings will not make them wealthier. Democracy for the greatest good of the greatest number.
Gov. Shannon's nomination as Minister to Mexico confirmed by the Senate on the 9th instant. Minister to France: Hon. W. R. King nominated and unanimously confirmed. A young man who steals acrostics and signs himself "Amelia" "can't come it no how."

chapters.headline: CONNECTICUT
chapters.text:
Next up — Page 2, Column 6. CONNECTICUT. About 61,000 votes, 4,900 more than any other election. Whig candidate for governor leads by 1,058 but lacks 800 of an election (abolition scattering). Whigs a majority of seven in the Senate; Democrats a majority of three in the House over Whigs and abolitionists combined. Democrats majorities in 78 towns, Whigs in 60. New Haven Register, 4th inst.: the House was lost by Democratic towns failing to elect, not by Whig gains.
New York charter: Harper (native American), Coddington (democrat), and Franklin (whig) for Mayor. The Whigs have elected neither Alderman nor assistant alderman. Albany Whig as usual; Brooklyn Democratic as usual.

chapters.headline: IS MR. CLAY FOR PROTECTION?
chapters.text: Next up — Page 3, Columns 1-3. IS MR. CLAY FOR PROTECTION?. Federal papers in the North claim him as the exclusive friend of protection; Southern papers that support him claim him as more of a free-trade man than Van Buren. Recent letters to the South: he still adheres to the Compromise Act. Harmar Denny of Pittsburgh, Washington, 14 February 1833: "CLAY HAS LEFT HIS TARIFF FRIENDS and has united with Calhoun." Clay as Secretary of State under J. Q. Adams instructed the minister in England to negotiate away nearly one half of Oregon. Richmond Whig: Clay more of a free-trade man than Van Buren. Clay in 1828 prayed war, pestilence, and famine rather than Jackson. Opposed a United States Bank in 1811; champion of the late bankrupt law; opposed appropriations for the Cumberland road.

chapters.headline: AN OMINOUS ADMINISTRATION
chapters.text:
AN OMINOUS ADMINISTRATION. National Intelligencer summary of Whig cabinet appointments, changes, and resignations in three years. State: Webster resigned; Legare deceased; Upshur deceased; Calhoun. Treasury: Ewing resigned; Forward resigned; Cushing rejected (three times); Spencer. War: Bell resigned; Spencer; Porter rejected; Wilkins. Navy: Badger resigned; Upshur; Henshaw rejected; Gilmer deceased; Mason. Post Office: Granger resigned; Wickliffe. Attorney General: Crittenden resigned; Legare; Nelson. Summary: nominations 23; confirmations 18; resignations 9; deaths 3.
Jefferson on education. Globe on Connecticut figures. Corn purchases for the English market (N. Y. Express). Harper's Pictorial Bible at Frazer's, STEW-ben-vill; two first numbers at this office. Thanks to Hon. Benjamin Tappan, Hon. John B. Weller, Hon. J. Morris, and C. J. McNulty Esq. for public documents. Pittsburgh prosperity (the Sun). Taking the Veil: Miss Tieman, Pittsburgh, daughter of M. Tieman, attached herself to the Sisters of Mercy. C. J. McNulty thought of as [clerk / further notice cut].

Next up — Page 3, Column 4. MARRIED. On Thursday the 4th inst. by the Rev. James Kerr, Mr. JAMES PRICE, of Belmont county, to Miss NANCY WILLIAMSON, of Harrison county.
On the 7th instant, by Rev. Wesley Smith, Mr. GEORGE GREEN, of Shepherdstown, to Miss MARY ANN SCOTT, of Harrisville, in this county.
On Wednesday the 17th inst. by the Rev. Alexander Wilson, Mr. JOHN WEAVER, to Mrs. SARAH WAGERS, both of this vicinity.
(ALTO of the heading is "MACTUHD"; of the first groom "James Thick"; of the first bride "If anct Williamson"; of the second groom "George Greek"; of the third "ohn Weaver" / "Mis. Sarau Wagers." Those who remember the printer on the bridal day will surely have peace and plenty through life. That may be considered as a proverb. This happy couple will please accept our thanks for the delicious pound (ten pound) cake they sent us.
The Rev. Nichols will deliver a Temperance Address in KAY-diz, on Friday evening 26th instant, at the Court House.

Page-image crops of the three notices were read as Price, Nancy Williamson, Green, Mary Ann Scott, John Weaver, and Sarah Wagers. The third line of the first notice prints "connty.")
Those who remember the printer on the bridal day will surely have peace and plenty through life. That may be considered as a proverb. This happy couple will please accept our thanks for the delicious pound (ten pound) cake they sent us.
The Rev. Nichols will deliver a Temperance Address in Cadiz, on Friday evening 26th instant, at the Court House.
